text: Electronic warfare (EW; Ukrainian REB, radioelektronna borotba) has set the terms of the drone war in Ukraine since 2022.
RUSI's Ukrainian-sourced data showed that about 90% of the UAS Ukraine employed in 2022 were lost.

metric_new.label: Share of drones employed that are lost

text: RUSI's Ukrainian-sourced data for 2022 showed EW to be the main counter-UAS tool.
RUSI's 2022 lessons say precision weapons "can be defeated by EW".

In the Ukraine war a recurring pattern is that a new capability arrives and dominates; examples are GMLRS, Excalibur, commercial quadcopters, analogue FPVs, Starlink, Shahed, fibre-optic FPVs, interceptor drones and mesh-controlled jet Gerans.
notes: Uncited synthesis in the research file; cited source is the one the overview paragraph gives for the start of the pattern.

text: In the recurring pattern, the other side then finds the new capability's physical-layer weakness, such as the GNSS signal, the control or video frequency, the satellite link, the emitter signature, the cable or speed.
notes: Uncited synthesis in the research file; cited source is the one the overview paragraph gives for the start of the pattern.

text: In the recurring pattern, the counter is cheap, spreads fast and forces a counter-counter; examples are moving frequencies, CRPA antennas, fibre, autonomy, whitelists, mesh relays, nets, jet engines and digital video.
notes: Uncited synthesis in the research file; cited source is the one the overview paragraph gives for the start of the pattern.

text: In some weeks of 2023 more than 2,000 Ukrainian drones were disabled.
Russia blunted US GPS-guided munitions in 2023: Excalibur's hit rate fell from 55% to 6%.
In 2024–25 fibre-optic FPVs and CRPA antennas shifted the EW edge back to Russia.
Russia fielded fibre-optic FPVs first, from August 2024 in Kursk.
Russia moved to multi-element CRPA antennas (Kometa-M) to beat Ukrainian GNSS jamming.
A Ukrainian EW company commander dates the "collapse" of conventional frontline jamming to the end of 2024.
In 2025 Ukraine answered in several ways at once: mass EW production, GNSS jamming and spoofing, interceptor drones, terminal autonomy and nets over logistics roads.
Ukrainian EW output rose 340-fold in 2024, from more than 140 makers.
Lima is the backbone of Ukraine's national Pokrova GNSS jamming and spoofing system.
Ukrainian interceptor drones were used first against Russian reconnaissance UAVs and then against Shaheds.
In 2025 Ukraine added terminal autonomy (TFL-1) to its drones.
In 2025 Ukraine put nets over logistics roads.
In February 2026 the Starlink whitelist cut Russia off from the satellite link that had become the backbone of its drone and assault C2; it was the biggest single swing in the EW contest.
Biletsky put the drop in Russian drone effectiveness at 20–40% in the first two weeks after the Starlink cut in February 2026.

text: In the 2026 strike war, jet Gerans outran the cheap Ukrainian propeller interceptors.
At the tactical radio-frequency level, EW change in Ukraine is monthly or faster.
Ukrainian vehicle jammers got by with one standard 900 MHz module until spring 2024, then needed four to five modules by summer 2024 and seven by autumn 2024.
Captured Russian FPV chips cover 300–1100 MHz, so a band change is a firmware update, not new hardware.
The "Firmware 1001" used to fly DJI quadcopters in war conditions went through more than 40 versions in two years, about one every two to three weeks.

text: The Excalibur 55% → 6% drop is the Washington Post's reading of internal Ukrainian data; some secondary summaries say "70% → 6%", which the research file could not find in RUSI's text.

The Starlink cut is dated 1 February 2026 (ISW, 26 Feb), 2 February (the cabinet resolution) and 5 February (terminals blocked; Ukrinform, and ISW as relayed by Euromaidan); the whitelist was phased, so all are defensible.

Reported gains after the Starlink cut range from 10–12 km (Wikipedia, southern front) to more than 200 km² (Atlantic Council); they use different units, depth of advance and area retaken, so they don't directly conflict but need a common measure such as DeepStateMap's monthly km² statistics.
Biletsky's 20–40% effectiveness drop is the only measured effect of the Starlink cut on Russian drone output.
On the Russian anti-Starlink effect, a Russian industry source claims Volna has "shut down Starlink" wherever needed, while a Ukrainian engineer measures 0–35% packet loss.
The Lima Kinzhal counts (41 of 42 in April, 61 by July 2026) and "KABs to zero" all come from the developer and the Night Watch unit that fields Lima, and Hambling flags them as unverified.
Interceptor-share figures vary with scope (one night, the Kyiv region or a month), and official "shot down/suppressed" totals lump kinetic and EW kills together.

ISW counts 12 working Rassvet satellites giving up to 90 minutes a day in total, while Euromaidan's tracking-based count is two windows of more than an hour each; both give a working altitude of about 550 km.
